question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{7\cdot 7-12\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -12 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -12 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -12 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
